payout_quote: Take steps each day to save water and protect the environment by choosing WaterSense labeled products in your home, yard, and business.
timing: Varies by utility offer: typically a bill credit or rebate check within weeks of documented purchase and installation.
eligibility: Set by each local utility's rebate offer: generally must be a residential customer of the participating water utility and purchase a WaterSense labeled product (toilets, showerheads, faucets, irrigation controllers, etc.).
catches: Rebates are utility-specific — many water utilities offer nothing, so a large share of users get $0.
Every rebate requires buying the fixture first — a discount on spending, not money earned.
Typical rebates are $25-$100 per fixture; the $500 top end is not representative.
The product must carry the WaterSense label; efficient but unlabeled products do not qualify.
steps: Go to https://www.epa.gov/watersense and use the 'Find Rebates' link to look up offers from your water utility.
Confirm the offer is currently live, the qualifying WaterSense labeled products, and any pre-approval requirement.
Buy and install the qualifying fixture and keep the receipt.
Submit the utility's rebate form with proof of purchase; the rebate arrives as a bill credit or check.
biggest_catch: Real EPA rebate directory, but rebates are utility-specific (many areas have none) and require buying the fixture first — typically $25-$100 back, not $500; it is a discount, not income.
